literal: Those who speak, all that they speak, is the fame that stands upon those who give something to those who beg.
translation: Of all the words spoken by those who speak, the only praise that endures is the fame of those who give to the needy.
modern: புகழ்ந்து பேசுபவர்கள் பேசும் புகழுரைகள் எல்லாம், இரப்பவர்க்கு ஏதேனும் ஒன்றை வாரி வழங்குபவர்களின் மேல் நிலைத்து நிற்கும் புகழே ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate source of lasting fame. The poet states that among all the topics and praises spoken by people, the only true praise that endures is the fame of those who give generously. The word 'ஈவார்' refers to those who give, and 'இரப்பார்' refers to those who ask or beg. The fame ('புகழ்') of such givers stands ('நிற்கும்') above all other subjects of human speech, making charity the highest virtue worthy of praise.
